answer: One optician grinds each mirror, and the polishing log counts every stroke of every session, signed at the end of each night. A trellis mirror bought from a distant shop fails the log: at the ledge of the glass the stroke pattern must match the optician's own hand, and a shop mirror carries another worker's marks. Copying the record means grinding glass for six months, faking 90 nightly entries and paying 16,200, and the tundra signature etched on the mirror's edge is read before every viewing, so a mirror whose strokes were never logged is shelved.
